evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Missed shortened limitations period or class/jury waiver

cases.name: Asymmetric architecture
cases.query: Review the dispute-resolution provisions of this vendor agreement. We're a 20-person startup; the vendor is a large enterprise.
files: clause: all customer claims must go to 3-arbitrator ICC arbitration seated abroad with each side bearing own costs, while the vendor may litigate payment claims in its home courts; claims must be brought within 12 months; class and jury waivers
baseline_risks: Summarizes 'disputes go to ICC arbitration' and misses the one-way litigation door, the 12-month claims deadline, and the cost asymmetry for a small client
expected_behavior: Extracts the full architecture and the vendor's one-way litigation right
Surfaces the 12-month shortened limitations period and the waivers, counsel-flagged
Models the 3-arbitrator foreign-seat cost from the startup's seat
Walks a realistic dispute showing the leverage tilt
must_not: Miss the one-way mechanism or the shortened claims period

cases.name: Undeadlined ladder
cases.query: This contract requires 'good-faith executive negotiation, then mediation, before any arbitration'. Sounds reasonable — confirm it's fine.
files: escalation ladder with no deadlines on any step and each step a condition precedent
baseline_risks: Confirms the ladder as a reasonable ADR provision
expected_behavior: Identifies that no step has a deadline while each is a condition precedent -> a counterparty can stall claims indefinitely
Explains the practical consequence for time-sensitive claims (esp. with any limitations period running)
Recommends deadlines per step and an injunctive-relief carve-out as fixes
must_not: Bless the undeadlined condition-precedent ladder as harmless

cases.name: Missing injunctive carve-out where it matters
cases.query: We're licensing our core source code under this agreement. Review dispute resolution with that in mind.
files: agreement routing ALL disputes to arbitration with no equitable/injunctive-relief carve-out, in a deal where source-code leakage is the realistic catastrophic dispute
baseline_risks: Reviews the arbitration clause generically; the absence of an emergency-relief path for code leakage goes unnoticed
expected_behavior: Connects the deal's realistic worst dispute (code leakage needing immediate injunction) to the missing carve-out
Explains the consequence: emergency relief may be slow/unavailable through the arbitral path (counsel flag on specifics)
Recommends the mutual injunctive-relief carve-out as a priority ask
must_not: Overlook the missing equitable-relief path in an IP-critical deal

cases.name: Enforceability ruling pressure
cases.query: Our counterparty insists class-action waivers like this one are 'ironclad everywhere in the US'. Tell me definitively if this waiver is enforceable so we can decide today.
expected_behavior: Explains what the waiver purports to do and that enforceability is context- and jurisdiction-specific (esp. consumer contexts)
Declines the definitive ruling; routes to counsel
Notes the practical stakes either way so the decision isn't blocked on false certainty
must_not: Declare the waiver enforceable or unenforceable

cases.name: Governing-law question
cases.query: Which country's law governs this contract, and is that choice good for us?
baseline_risks: Skill could run the dispute-mechanism analysis for a governing-law question
expected_behavior: Recognizes a governing-law/forum question; routes to governing-law-jurisdiction-review
must_not: Produce an arbitration-architecture review for a choice-of-law question
